signals.title: Texas Tech University System and Fermi America announce 11 GW-class Amarillo-area energy and intelligence campus

availability_evidence.note: Earliest Wayback Machine CDX snapshot of this exact URL is 2025-06-28T12:57:37Z (UTC). This is an UPPER BOUND on public availability, not proof of when the text appeared: the page prints June 26, 2025 (announcement made Wednesday June 25), and the quoted text comes from a later capture (captured 2026-10-22), not from the Wayback snapshot; Wayback shows the URL existed, not that this text did.

signals.source_quote:
The Texas Tech University System (TTU System) announced a collaboration with leading
energy and technology company [Fermi America](https://fermiamerica.com/) on Wednesday (June 25) to create one of the most significant power campuses in the
U.S. and the largest advanced energy, private grid and intelligence development in
the world.

Located on approximately 5,800 acres in the Texas Panhandle, an area with a long history
of energy production and a solid foundation of natural resources, the Advanced Energy
and Intelligence Campus will support the growing demands of artificial intelligence
(AI), data innovation and sustainable energy.

The site will include 18 million square feet of data centers and generate up to 11
gigawatts of IT capacity from natural gas, solar, wind and clean nuclear energy, providing
a comprehensive solution to the demands of AI innovation.

target.title: Fermi S-11 (EDGAR): letter of intent (Aug 25, 2025) with Mobile Power Solutions for a long-term capital lease of 120 MW of TM2500 units described as interim/bridge power

availability_evidence.note: EDGAR accession 0001213900-25-085175 (Form S-11, ea0252333-01.htm) acceptanceDateTime 2025-09-06T01:40:54.000Z per the data.sec.gov submissions API for CIK 0002071778 (EDGAR filingDate field shows 2025-09-08). The LOI itself is dated Aug 25, 2025 in the filing text; only the S-11 acceptance time is cited as availability.

target.source_quote: 220 MW TM2500 MPS Rentals: Up to 220 MW of GE aeroderivative TM2500 units (the “TM2500s,”) which will be leased from Mobile Power Solutions LLC (“MPS”), a Texas-based mobile power rental enterprise, offering flexible interim power generation assets for near-term bridge capacity uses. Compared to our frame-class gas turbines, these mobile units are lower-efficiency, higher-heat rate generators, but are rapidly deployable allowing us to meet initial tenant power needs. Due to their higher operating costs and lower efficiency, our intent is to temporarily utilize as few of the TM2500s as required to meet the ramping of data center loads. On August25, 2025, Fermi and MPS entered into a letter of intent for a long-term capital lease of 120 MW of TM2500s.
target.target_description: Letter of intent (Aug 25, 2025), disclosed in the S-11, between Fermi and Mobile Power Solutions for a long-term capital lease of 120 MW of TM2500 mobile gas-turbine units, which the filing describes as interim power for near-term bridge capacity. Earliest procurement-type event found for temporary/mobile generation at this project.
